strings.d1.s0.name: Taipei 101 Observatory
strings.d1.s0.tips: Floor 89. The first slot in the morning is uncrowded. Look for the wind damper ball.
strings.d1.s1.name: Xinyi District
strings.d1.s1.tips: Shopping malls and the Eslite bookstore, all air-conditioned.
strings.d1.s2.name: Din Tai Fung Xinyi
strings.d1.s2.tips: The brand that made xiaolongbao (soup dumplings) famous. Take a queue number at 11:45.
strings.d1.s3.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
strings.d1.s3.tips: Changing of the guard every hour. The park has views of Taipei 101.
strings.d1.s4.name: Elephant Mountain
strings.d1.s4.tips: A steep 20-minute staircase climb. The sunset photo of Taipei 101 is crowded but worth it.
strings.d1.b0.name: Kao Chi Yongkang
strings.d1.b0.tips: A cheaper rival to Din Tai Fung, serving xiaolongbao.
strings.d1.b1.name: Songshan Cultural Park
strings.d1.b1.tips: Design exhibitions in an old tobacco factory.
strings.d2.s0.name: National Palace Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: Imperial Chinese treasures, including the Jadeite Cabbage and the Meat-shaped Stone, Tuesday to Saturday. Go before the morning tour buses arrive.
strings.d2.s1.name: Shilin Official Residence
strings.d2.s1.tips: The gardens of Chiang Kai-shek's residence, with a rose garden.
strings.d2.s2.name: Lin Dong Fang Beef Noodle
strings.d2.s2.tips: Some of the best beef noodle soup in Taipei (Bib Gourmand), with a clear broth.
strings.d2.s3.name: Beitou Thermal Valley
strings.d2.s3.tips: A steaming green hot spring lake with a sulphur smell. Take the MRT to Xinbeitou.
strings.d2.s4.name: Beitou Public Hot Spring
strings.d2.s4.tips: A public hot spring (60 TWD, swimwear required), shared with locals.
strings.d2.b0.name: Shilin Night Market
strings.d2.b0.tips: Taipei's biggest night market, known for giant fried chicken cutlets and stinky tofu.
strings.d2.b1.name: Beitou Hot Spring Museum
strings.d2.b1.tips: A Japanese-era bathhouse building, good for a rainy day.
strings.d3.s0.name: Yehliu Geopark
strings.d3.s0.tips: See the Queen's Head rock and the mushroom rocks. Arrive before the tour buses.
strings.d3.s1.name: Shifen Waterfall
strings.d3.s1.tips: Known as Taiwan's Niagara. A 20-minute walk.
strings.d3.s2.name: Shifen Old Street
strings.d3.s2.tips: Release a sky lantern over the railway tracks (150 TWD) and watch the trains pass.
strings.d3.s3.name: Jiufen Old Street
strings.d3.s3.tips: A terraced mountain town with taro balls and tea houses, and a Spirited Away feel.
strings.d3.s4.name: A-Mei Tea House Jiufen
strings.d3.s4.tips: A tea house hung with red lanterns. Come for the oolong and the view; the lanterns light up at sunset.
strings.d3.b0.name: Jiufen Grandma Lai Taro Ball
strings.d3.b1.name: Houtong Cat Village
strings.d3.b1.tips: A cat village, as an alternative to Shifen.
strings.d4.s0.name: Longshan Temple
strings.d4.s0.tips: Taipei's oldest temple. Come in the morning for prayers, incense and divination blocks.
strings.d4.s1.name: Bopiliao Historic Block
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Qing-era street with a free exhibition.
strings.d4.s2.name: Dihua Street
strings.d4.s2.tips: Dadaocheng's street of dried goods and tea, with Baroque facades and a Lunar New Year market.
strings.d4.s3.name: Yongle Market Food Court
strings.d4.s3.tips: Local food in the Dadaocheng market. Try the oyster omelette.
strings.d4.s4.name: Dadaocheng Wharf
strings.d4.s4.tips: Riverside container bars, with sunset views and cycling.
strings.d4.b0.name: Du Hsiao Yueh Taipei
strings.d4.b1.name: Ximending
strings.d4.b1.tips: Taipei's Shibuya, with youth culture and street art. A swap for the wharf.
strings.d5.s0.name: Yangmingshan Qingtiangang
strings.d5.s0.tips: Grassland and water buffalo above the city. Cool in summer. Take bus 260.
strings.d5.s1.name: Xiaoyoukeng
strings.d5.s1.tips: Sulphur fumaroles and views of Qixing Mountain.
strings.d5.s2.name: Yangmingshan Zhuzihu
strings.d5.s2.tips: Calla lily fields and a village restaurant.
strings.d5.s3.name: Yangmingshan Kalla Restaurant
strings.d5.s3.tips: Mountain vegetables and chicken in Zhuzihu.
strings.d5.s4.name: Raohe Night Market
strings.d5.s4.tips: A single-street night market. The charcoal-baked pepper buns (Fuzhou pepper buns) are at the entrance.
strings.d5.b0.name: Ningxia Night Market
strings.d5.b1.name: Xiangshan
strings.d6.s0.name: Tamsui Old Street
strings.d6.s0.tips: At the end of the MRT line, an estuary town known for a-gei (stuffed tofu) and fish balls.
strings.d6.s1.name: Fort San Domingo
strings.d6.s1.tips: A Dutch-Spanish fort and British consulate. Look for the red building.
strings.d6.s2.name: Tamsui A-Gei Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.tips: Glass noodles stuffed in tofu, Tamsui's signature dish.
strings.d6.s3.name: Fisherman's Wharf Tamsui
strings.d6.s3.tips: Lovers' Bridge. Cross by ferry; there are cafes on the pier.
strings.d6.s4.name: Tamsui Sunset Beach
strings.d6.s4.tips: Home to some of Taiwan's most famous sunsets, over the estuary.
strings.d6.b0.name: Tamsui Zhengzhong Fish Ball
strings.d6.b1.name: Bali Left Bank
strings.d6.b1.tips: The opposite bank by ferry, with a cycle path.
strings.d7.s0.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
strings.d7.s0.tips: A giant white monument with a changing of the guard every hour. Liberty Square is out front.
strings.d7.s1.name: Yongkang Street
strings.d7.s1.tips: Cafes and mango shaved ice. Try Smoothie House.
strings.d7.s2.name: Yongkang Beef Noodle
strings.d7.s2.tips: Serving braised beef noodles since 1963. A good farewell lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: Da'an Forest Park
strings.d7.s3.tips: A city forest for a last walk. The MRT to Taoyuan Airport takes 40 minutes.
strings.d7.b0.name: Smoothie House Yongkang
strings.d7.b0.tips: Mango snow ice, a dessert in place of noodles.
strings.d7.b1.name: Taipei Botanical Garden
strings.d7.b1.tips: Lotus ponds, as a swap for the park.
strings.note0: EasyCard works on the MRT, buses and YouBike. Eating and drinking are banned on the MRT (you will be fined). The MRT to Taoyuan Airport takes 40 minutes.
strings.note1: Summer brings 33°C heat and humidity, and July to September carries a typhoon risk (everything closes under a T8 signal). Sightsee in the morning, visit museums or malls in the afternoon, and go to night markets in the cooler evening.
strings.note2: Night markets run 18:00-24:00, and 300 TWD is enough to eat your fill. Tipping is not expected, and cash is still widely used.
strings.note3: For Jiufen, Shifen and Yehliu, take a tour (~1,500 TWD) or bus 1062. Go to Jiufen in the afternoon, as the lanterns light up after 17:00.
strings.note4: Take a queue number at Din Tai Fung. Noodles at Yongkang and Lin Dong Fang cost 250 TWD.
strings.note5: You do not take your shoes off in temples. Divination blocks and incense are open to all.
strings.transit.name: EasyCard
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on the MRT, buses, YouBike and in convenience stores, including the Jiufen bus
